title: Box Elder: Ancient Box Elders You Can Visit
meta_description: A weedy maple usually written off before it gets old. Three exceptions mapped, from Illinois's state champion to a Setubal survivor pushing 120.
intro: Box elder has a bad reputation. It seeds itself into alleys and vacant lots, drops limbs without warning, hosts the boxelder bugs that swarm into houses every autumn, and rarely gets the chance to grow old before someone cuts it down as a weed. It is also, unusually for a maple, compound-leafed: where every other Acer carries a single lobed leaf, this one splits its into three, five or seven separate leaflets, so people routinely mistake it for an ash. Three trees on this site are the exceptions that outlasted the reputation. Chicago's, on a public golf course in Edgebrook, is Illinois's state champion by the University of Illinois Extension's own scoring formula, undated but the biggest known in the state. Eindhoven's stands in a small parish churchyard, planted in the 1920s, and has outlived the congregation that put it there. Setubal's, at roughly 117 years old, is the oldest living thing in the city's main park, on ground that was open countryside when it was planted.
